intro.body: Set your dog and lifestyle profile, see an honest cost breakdown, take a short readiness quiz — then get a monthly budget, yearly forecast, and smart tips. Everything stays in the browser.

insights.dim-timeReadiness-high: Time availability looks solid — protect walk routines on hard days.
insights.dim-timeReadiness-low: Time is the bottleneck. Plan shifts/a walker before the dog arrives.
insights.dim-budgetBuffer-high: Emergency-budget awareness is strong — that saves pets and bank accounts.
insights.dim-budgetBuffer-low: Without a vet cushion, every surprise becomes a crisis. Start a small jar now.
insights.dim-spaceLifestyle-high: Home and routine look compatible — recheck on long workdays.
insights.dim-spaceLifestyle-low: Space/alone-time still misaligned. Enrich the environment or change the schedule.
insights.dim-commitment-high: You’re thinking long-term — dogs don’t move like furniture.
insights.dim-commitment-low: Multi-year commitment needs a plan for travel, moves, and life changes.
insights.overall-strong: The picture is stable — lock a monthly budget and review quarterly.
insights.overall-steady: Good base with soft spots — close one gap this week.
insights.overall-developing: Willingness is there; gaps are still large. Simplify before adopting.
insights.overall-needs-care: Signals say: prepare more. Waiting beats risking the dog’s welfare.
insights.size-small: Small dogs: cheaper food, but vet/grooming still add up.
insights.size-medium: Medium dogs: balance food, activity, and an emergency cushion.
insights.size-large: Large dogs: food, meds, and vet travel cost more — budget accordingly.
insights.age-puppy: Puppies: year one is pricier (vaccines, training, gear) — expect it.
insights.age-adult: Adults: steadier costs — keep prevention and annual checkups.
insights.age-senior: Seniors: medical follow-up rises — an emergency cushion matters more.
insights.alone-homeMostly: Someone home often — a big asset for calm and habits.
insights.alone-mixed: Mixed alone time: a goodbye routine + enrichment cuts anxiety and damage.
insights.alone-aloneOften: Alone a lot: walker/sitter/boarding is budget — not a luxury.

tips.tip-walk-blocks: Block two fixed walk windows like unmissable meetings.
tips.tip-rain-kit: A rain kit by the door (coat/towel) lowers ‘not today’ resistance.
tips.tip-shared-shifts: Write family walk shifts down — not chaotic chat threads.
tips.tip-emergency-jar: Auto-set aside a monthly vet fund — even a small amount helps.
tips.tip-buy-bulk: Buy quality food smartly (bulk/subscriptions) without cutting nutrition.
tips.tip-preventive-care: Prevention (parasites, teeth, weight) beats emergency bills.
tips.tip-enrichment: Food puzzles and enrichment reduce destruction when alone.
tips.tip-alone-routine: Practice short departures before a full workday.
tips.tip-neighbor-plan: Have a neighbor/family backup before you need it.
tips.tip-10-year-view: Ask: can we sustain this in 5–10 years?
tips.tip-boarding-list: Keep a boarding/walker backup list before the first trip.
tips.tip-vet-relationship: Pick a regular vet — continuity beats expensive guessing.
tips.tip-track-month: Track one real month of spend — then update the budget.
tips.tip-groom-diy: Between groomer visits: regular brushing cuts mats and cost.
tips.tip-food-quality: Don’t cheap out on core food — save on unnecessary luxury brands.

rainy-walks.prompt: On rainy/cold days — we still have time and willingness for a real walk.

options.1: On rainy days we cancel or just do a 2-minute yard pee break
options.2: We only go out if we must — shortest possible outing
options.3: Short walk with coat/towel — sometimes we skip
options.4: Rain kit by the door; we go out almost every time
options.5: A real walk in rain/cold is routine, not optional

daily-minutes.prompt: We have daily minutes for walks, play, and care — not only “later”.

bySize.small: We have daily time for walks/play even for a small, stim-hungry dog.
bySize.medium: We have enough daily time for a medium dog’s walks and activity.
bySize.large: We have serious daily time for longer walks with a large dog.

options.1: Barely 15 minutes — everything slips to the weekend
options.2: A short evening window that often gets canceled
options.3: About 30–45 minutes/day, with some missed busy days
options.4: Two walk/play windows on most weekdays
options.5: Daily time blocked on the calendar for walks, play, care

vet-bill-jump.prompt: If a vet bill suddenly jumps — we have a plan (cushion/credit) without panic.

options.1: No cushion — we’d scramble or delay care
options.2: Rely on credit with no prepared plan
options.4: Dog emergency fund or ready credit line
options.5: Dedicated cushion + clear rule for when we call the vet

monthly-buffer.prompt: We can cover the estimated monthly budget without straining the rest of the household.

options.1: The monthly estimate would stretch us hard
options.2: We’d manage, but other bills would suffer
options.3: Doable if we’re careful for a few months
options.4: Comfortable range with a small margin
options.5: Fits the household budget without crowding other needs

space-ok.prompt: Home/area space fits a dog for movement and rest.

bySize.small: There’s a safe corner and enough space for a small dog.
bySize.medium: Home and yard/area fit a medium dog.
bySize.large: There’s enough space and movement for a large dog — not only a cramped living room.

options.1: Urban studio with no balcony / very limited space
options.2: Small flat with a narrow balcony, weak park access
options.3: Apartment with elevator and a park/path nearby
options.4: Roomy flat or house with easy daily walk access
options.5: House with a fenced yard / clear space to move and rest

alone-plan.prompt: We have a clear plan for alone time (routine, enrichment, help).

options.1: No plan yet — we’ll see what happens
options.2: One toy and hope neighbors don’t complain
options.3: Basic goodbye routine, no backup on long workdays
options.5: Written routine: gradual alone training, enrichment, fixed backup

travel-cover.prompt: For trips we have boarding/sitter coverage or budget — not last-minute improvisation.

options.2: Hope family can help, nothing booked
options.3: Idea for boarding/sitter, no budget locked yet
options.5: Reserved spot / sitter agreement + dedicated travel budget

years-ahead.prompt: We’re thinking years ahead — not only the cute first months.

byAge.puppy: We’re ready for long commitment after the puppy phase too.
byAge.adult: We see the coming years with the dog as part of normal life.
byAge.senior: We’re ready for medical follow-up and age-related changes.

options.1: Mostly thinking about the next few months
options.2: Know it’s long-term, haven’t planned life changes
options.3: Talked 1–2 years ahead, not a decade
options.4: Thought through moves, trips, and job changes
options.5: Family agreement on multi-year commitment + scenarios

training-patience.prompt: We have patience for training and consistency — even when it doesn’t stick immediately.

byAge.puppy: We’re ready to invest time in puppy training (accidents included).
byAge.adult: We’re ready to work on habits with an adult dog too.
byAge.senior: We understand habit change in seniors needs gentleness.

options.1: Expect the dog to “just get it” quickly
options.2: Train a bit, then quit when there’s a setback
options.3: Train when we have time — inconsistent
options.4: Short, steady practice even when it repeats
options.5: Planned patience and consistency (trainer if needed)

family-aligned.prompt: Everyone at home is aligned on rules, care, and responsibility.

options.1: No alignment — everyone has different rules
options.2: We’ve talked, but roles are unclear
options.3: Mostly aligned, with a few friction points
options.4: Clear responsibility split across the household
options.5: Everyone agrees on the same rules: walks, food, boundaries
